main_text.p: libus ex professo agitur, judices non tantum non dicuntur Otiosi, sed ab iisdem etiam distinguuntur, uti ex Cod. Sanhedrin liquet, loco alibi à nobis citato.

X V. Sed si quid denique illud de Otiosis veri habeat, istud summum inde recte colligi poterit & concludi; usum vocis במלינים vel Otiosorum, tandem sequioribus seculis à Judæis Babyloniis ita ampliatum esse, ut ea præter Veterum morem etiam Doctores Academicos, eosdemque Iudices, fuerit complexa; haud secus ac חזן & שליח הציבור qui olim distincti fuerunt, à recentioribus plerisque ita confunduntur, ut hactenus Viri in his literis Principes illos putaverint eosdem. Id autem quicquid sit, nobis certe obesse non potest; nisi quis ita secum statuat, animumque credere inducat: Veterum Hebræorum ritus & mores ex hodiernorum quorundam sive errore, sive abusu vocis, contra constantem Doctissimorum quorumcunque Interpretum consensum, accipiendos & explicandos esse.

page.notes: Hebrew words in the line "usum vocis" and "qui olim distincti" are printed in Hebrew letters; the Hebrew for "במלינים" and "חזן ושליח הציבור" are copied as best legible and may be imperfect. The Hebrew "שליח הציבור" is set in a line with the words "& חזן". The "CA" signature is printed at the right; the scan shows the letters faintly. Greek and Hebrew transcriptions are uncertain where marked by the scan quality.
